claim: For connected finite simple undirected graphs compared at the same order \(n\) and the same size \(m\), algebraic connectivity \(a(G)=\lambda_2(L_G)\) and edge connectivity \(e(G)\) cannot give opposite strict robustness rankings for any pair with \(n\le5\). Order \(n=6\) is sharp: at \(m=7\), let \(A\) be the cone over \(P_3\cup2K_1\), and let \(B\) be a triangle and a \(4\)-cycle sharing exactly one vertex. Then \(e(A)=1<2=e(B)\), because \(A\) has bridges while \(B\) is \(2\)-edge-connected, but \(a(A)=1>3-\sqrt5=a(B)\). Thus the Fiedler value ranks the bridge-containing graph as more connected even after order and edge count are held fixed, while edge connectivity ranks the bridgeless graph as more robust to link deletion. The lower bound is exhaustive over all connected graph isomorphism classes through five vertices.
integrity: The lower bound is exhaustive over all connected graph isomorphism classes through five vertices. The packaged verifier generates those graphs from edge subsets, quotients by all vertex permutations, checks edge connectivity by all cuts, and compares exact Laplacian algebraic roots. The six-vertex witness has explicitly factored characteristic polynomials.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns connected finite simple undirected graphs, the combinatorial Laplacian, edge connectivity, and comparisons at common order and common edge count. It is a sharp finite boundary, not a classification of all larger reversals. Fiedler's 1973 source was inspected in full but the exact public day of that historical journal issue was not established; the exact archive-date anchor is the official 1 July 2009 publication date of the directly relevant network-robustness report.
title: Six vertices are the sharp fixed-density reversal boundary for algebraic and edge connectivity
